## reference · ph-internet-transactions-act-ra11967
* The Internet Transactions Act of 2023 aims to protect online consumers and merchants engaged in internet transactions.
* The Act applies to all business-to-business and business-to-consumer internet transactions within the Philippines.
* Online media content and consumer-to-consumer transactions are not covered under the Act.
* The E-Commerce Bureau will be created under the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) to regulate e-commerce.
* The Bureau will have powers to formulate policies, implement and monitor compliance, and investigate violations.
* Online merchants and digital platforms must register with the Bureau and submit necessary information.
* The Act ensures equal treatment of online and offline commercial activities.
* The DTI has regulatory jurisdiction over e-commerce, but must coordinate with other agencies such as the DICT, BSP, and NPC.
* The DTI Secretary has the power to issue subpoenas, compliance orders, and takedown orders.
* A takedown order can be issued for the removal of listings or offers of prohibited or regulated goods and services.
* The Act promotes consumer education and awareness on rights, responsibilities, and red flags in internet transactions.
* The Bureau will establish an Online Business Database (OBD) to provide access to contact information of online businesses.
* The DTI will encourage the development of an E-Commerce Philippine Trustmark to ensure safety and security in internet transactions.
Sources: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2023/ra_11967_2023.html
